co_d_the_badlands.blurb: The Badlands is a tall steep face of roughly 200 feet at high elevation within Staunton State Park, on the Black Creek Wall side of the South Platte. It holds about a dozen climbs, mostly bolted face lines with a pair of trad or mixed options, and a few routes stretch to two pitches. Grades centre on 5.10 and 5.11, with a handful of easier 5.9 climbs and a single 5.12 for the strong. The wall is near-vertical rather than slabby, so expect sustained, thoughtful face climbing. Climbing here is possible through much of the year, though a snow ledge at the base can complicate winter starts.

co_chernobyl.blurb: Chernobyl is a steep crag above Jackson Creek in the Devil's Head zone of the South Platte, about 8,900 feet up. A dozen routes split evenly between sport and trad, spanning roughly 5.7 to 5.11 with most of the difficulty around 5.8 to 5.10. The stone offers a mix of cracks, offwidths, chickenheads and patina, with a bit of pebble pinching, and one two-pitch moderate is known for outstanding views. The walk in is very short, a scramble of just a few minutes. Steep drops nearby make it a poor choice for small children or loose dogs.

co_deadwood_gulch.blurb: Deadwood Gulch is a small crag a few miles from Silverton, in the Animas River canyon along the Million Dollar Highway. It holds a dozen climbs, mostly traditional with a few bolted lines and a top-rope, and the grades are friendly: most fall between 5.6 and 5.8, with one 5.5 and a lone 5.10. The faces are orange and cut by horizontal cracks, with crisply fractured texture and some loose rock near the base. It is a quiet spot where shade is scarce, so afternoon sun can bake the wall; start early and bring water.

co_dance_hall_of_the_dead.blurb: Dance Hall of the Dead is a south-facing canyon slab in the South Fork of St. Vrain Canyon west of Lyons. It has a dozen climbs, mostly trad with three bolted lines, running from about 5.7 to 5.10, with the bulk at 5.9 and 5.10. Wide and thin cracks split the slab, and anchors on top make it a handy top-rope spot. Because it faces south, it feels harsh on sunny summer afternoons and best on cooler days. The rock was still a little mossy and flaky, and rattlesnakes are possible, so watch your step on the walk in.

co_engine_boulder.blurb: Engine Boulder is one of four boulders in the Freight Yard group on Nine Mile Hill, in Unaweep Canyon near Grand Junction, at about 4,750 feet. It carries a dozen problems, the most of any boulder there, and almost all are friendly: seven at V1, four around V3 and a single V4. The north face has a sit start under an overhang, a big chicken-head hold and a slab topped by juniper branches. The group is described as a convenient canyon spot with good landings, so a pad or two is plenty.
